pr.title: [beta] backports
pr.description:
- Emit specific message for `time<0.3.35` inference failure #129343
- Use a reduced recursion limit in the MIR inliner's cycle breaker #129714
- rustdoc: do not run doctests with invalid langstrings #128838 

r? cuviper
pr.author: cuviper

analysis.originalLogic: `mir_callgraph_reachable` in the MIR inliner used the crate's full trait-solving recursion budget (`tcx.recursion_limit()`) as the recursion budget for its call-graph reachability walk (`process`).
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Passing the full `tcx.recursion_limit()` into the inliner's call-graph cycle/reachability search causes the trait solver invoked while recursing into the call graph to hit the limit first and emit a fatal error, instead of the inliner gracefully giving up. The fix instead computes `let recursion_limit = tcx.recursion_limit() / 2;` so the inliner hits its own reduced limit first and abandons inlining.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust crates compiled with the next trait solver (`-Znext-solver`) that contain recursive or deep call graphs where trait-solving type complexity grows with call-graph depth, as in the code referenced by issue #128887. Shallow call graphs are not expected to hit either limit. The change is described as a time-boxed workaround.
analysis.summary: The MIR inliner's cycle-breaker search must not use the same recursion limit as the trait solver under `-Znext-solver`: doing so lets the solver overflow fatally first. The backported fix halves the inliner's recursion budget so the cycle breaker gives up on inlining rather than producing a fatal solver error.
analysis.trigger: MIR inlining cycle detection (`mir_callgraph_reachable`/`process`) recursively walks a call graph while invoking trait solving, with the next trait solver enabled; each recursion level increases the type complexity handed to the solver.
preconditions: MIR inliner is running call-graph reachability/cycle detection via `mir_callgraph_reachable`
The new trait solver (`-Znext-solver`) is in use
Call-graph recursion is deep enough for type-solving complexity to approach the recursion limit
Before the fix, the cycle breaker and the trait solver share the same recursion limit
pitfalls: Using the full recursion limit makes solver overflow a fatal error rather than a graceful inlining bailout
The halved limit can make the inliner miss useful deep inlining; the patch notes that needing to recurse 64 times is unlikely to find useful MIR inlining
The change is an explicit `FIXME(-Znext-solver)` hack intended to be removed once trait solver overflow can return an error
No regression test for this inliner change is included in this backport patch; the added tests instead cover the `time` inference diagnostic and rustdoc invalid langstrings
Do not conflate this MIR inliner cycle-breaker limit with `ForceInline` or with a change to inlining profitability decisions
analysis.testStrategy: Construct two compilations of the same deeply recursive generic call graph under `-Znext-solver`, differing only in the recursion budget passed by `mir_callgraph_reachable` to `process` (full `tcx.recursion_limit()` versus `tcx.recursion_limit() / 2`). Check that the full-budget variant can hit a fatal trait-solver overflow while the halved-budget variant compiles by abandoning the cycle search, and separately verify a shallow call graph still permits inlining. This is an inferred test design; no compiler was built, and the supplied patch adds no regression test for this hunk.
evidence: - Use a reduced recursion limit in the MIR inliner's cycle breaker #129714
